game.title: South Park: The Stick of Truth
game.blurb: Comedy role-playing game set in the town of South Park, from Obsidian Entertainment, released 2014-03-04. RAWG average playtime: 12 hours. Genres: Adventure, RPG. Chapters are an estimate drawn from Steam achievement themes.

chapters.title: The Main Story
chapters.summary: The New Kid moves to town and gets caught up in a make-believe war over a stick. Spoiler-guarded.

chapters.title: Friends and Exploring Town
chapters.summary: Making friends around town, Chinpokomon, garages, costumes and the odd places you can reach.

chapters.title: Fart Magic
chapters.summary: Farts in and out of battle, and the other toilet-humour achievements.

chapters.title: Battles, Buddies and Bosses
chapters.summary: Blocking, perfect attacks, buddies, upgrades and special ways to beat certain bosses.

chapters.title: Whole-Game Challenges
chapters.summary: Goals that span a full playthrough, such as never selling an item.

attribution: Achievement data from Steam (Steam Web API, app 213670)
StrategyWiki: no usable walkthrough, nothing used — https://strategywiki.org/wiki/South_Park:_The_Stick_of_Truth
Fandom (southpark.fandom.com, CC BY-SA): page names only were checked to confirm structure; no text copied — https://southpark.fandom.com/wiki/South_Park:_The_Stick_of_Truth
notes: Backlog game, picked from RAWG's most-added list for its year (docs/PLAN.md section 2 ordering). StrategyWiki has a page at completion stage 0: its Table of Contents lists Day 1 to Day 3 and Nights 1 and 2 as walkthrough sections, but none of those is written; only Abilities, Achievements and trophies, Classes, Controls, Magic, Summons and the Table of Contents exist. southpark.fandom.com answers the API, with about 126 linked pages; names only were looked at, nothing copied. 11 of 50 Steam achievements are hidden; they sit in the main story chapter as a placeholder, though low-rate ones such as "Inside Joke", "Face Hoff", "Two Girls, One Stick", "Perverted" and "Too Far" may be optional. Several descriptions use crude words (the game's own text) and are shown as written by Steam.
